tool.name: GWASLab Reference Download
tool.description: Prepare Galaxy-managed reference bundles for harmonization and rsID workflows
tool.command: python '$__tool_directory__/run_reference_download.py' --mode '$mode_selector.mode' #if str($mode_selector.mode) == "preset" --preset-name '$mode_selector.preset_name' --build '$mode_selector.build' --population '$mode_selector.population' --dbsnp-version '$mode_selector.dbsnp_version' #elif str($mode_selector.mode) == "keywords" --keywords '$mode_selector.keywords' #elif str($mode_selector.mode) == "local" --local-primary '$mode_selector.local_primary' --local-primary-label '$mode_selector.local_primary_label' #if $mode_selector.local_secondary --local-secondary '$mode_selector.local_secondary' --local-secondary-label '$mode_selector.local_secondary_label' #end if #if $mode_selector.local_tertiary --local-tertiary '$mode_selector.local_tertiary' --local-tertiary-label '$mode_selector.local_tertiary_label' #end if #if $mode_selector.local_quaternary --local-quaternary '$mode_selector.local_quaternary' --local-quaternary-label '$mode_selector.local_quaternary_label' #end if #end if --output-bundle '$output_bundle' --output-manifest '$output_manifest' --output-inventory '$output_inventory' --log '$log'

param.name: dbsnp_version
param.label: dbSNP version for full rsID bundles

tool.help:
This tool prepares Galaxy-managed reference bundles for later harmonization and rsID tools. It is meant to solve a practical Galaxy problem: GWASLab can download and register references in its own data directory, but Galaxy workflows need visible, reproducible outputs that can be passed from one tool to the next.
What the tool does:
- downloads curated GWASLab references into a temporary working directory - copies the selected files into a Galaxy output bundle instead of leaving them in a hidden user cache - writes a JSON manifest describing each reference and its intended downstream role - writes a tabular inventory so you can quickly inspect the bundle in Galaxy history
What the outputs mean:
- `reference bundle`: a tar.gz archive containing the packaged FASTA, VCF, TSV, and index files - `manifest`: machine-readable JSON for later tools to interpret - `inventory`: a flat table listing each bundled resource, its role, and original filename - `log`: a human-readable execution summary
Why bundle references instead of only downloading them to disk:
- Galaxy tracks the bundle as an output dataset, which is easier to reproduce - we avoid depending on a hidden per-user GWASLab download directory - downstream tools can consume a documented manifest instead of guessing file roles
Modes:
- `preset`: download a curated bundle for harmonization or rsID workflows - `keywords`: download an explicit list of GWASLab reference keywords - `local`: package existing FASTA/VCF/TSV files that are already in Galaxy history
Preset design choices:
- lightweight rsID bundles include the smaller `1kg_dbsnp151_*_auto` table - full rsID bundles also include a dbSNP VCF for broader variant coverage - harmonization bundles include a reference FASTA and a population-specific 1KG VCF
Typical usage:
- use `harmonization` when you are preparing for allele checking and strand inference - use `assign_rsid_light` when you mainly need CHR/POS to rsID mapping and want a smaller bundle - use `assign_rsid_full` when you want broader rsID coverage from dbSNP VCF resources - use `local` when the reference files already exist in Galaxy history and you just want them bundled with a manifest
Testing locally:
```bash planemo test tools/reference_download/tool.xml ```
